findings.title: Database connection never initialized in connect()
findings.description: The connect() method calls init_db() but never assigns a connection to self._db. Every call to _get_db() creates a new database connection instead of reusing one.
findings.evidence: async def connect(self) -> None: await init_db() # Missing: self._db = await get_db()
findings.consequence: Resource exhaustion under load due to connection leaks
findings.fix: Add 'self._db = await get_db()' after await init_db() in connect()

findings.title: Unreachable code in count_all() and count_for_user()
findings.description: count_all() is missing a return statement entirely. count_for_user() has two return statements with the second being unreachable.
findings.evidence:
async def count_all(self) -> int: ... # No return statement
async def count_for_user(self, user_id: int) -> int: ... return int(row["cnt"]) if row else 0
    return int(row["count"]) if row else 0
findings.consequence: count_all() returns None instead of integer; count_for_user() may return incorrect values
findings.fix: Add missing return statement to count_all() and remove unreachable return in count_for_user()

findings.title: Missing job type validation
findings.description: The run() method processes any job without checking job["type"] == "index_document".
findings.evidence: if job: await self._process_job(job) # No type check
findings.consequence: Worker processes any job type with indexing logic, potentially corrupting data

findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability in _sanitize_path
findings.description: _sanitize_path uses Path(storage_path).name which strips the directory path. Only the filename is used, losing the user-specific subdirectory.
findings.evidence: resolved = base_dir / Path(storage_path).name # Only uses .name, discarding directory
findings.consequence: Workers read incorrect files or fail; documents from different users get mixed up
findings.fix: Use (base_dir / storage_path).resolve() and validate relative_to instead of using .name

findings.title: Missing is_deleted column in database schema
findings.description: count_for_user() queries documents.is_deleted column that may not exist in schema.
findings.evidence: WHERE user_id = ? AND is_deleted = FALSE # Column not in documented schema
findings.consequence: Database query fails if migration not applied; soft-delete not implemented
findings.fix: Add is_deleted column via migration or remove from query

findings.title: Inconsistent database commit patterns
findings.description: _update_status() commits immediately, breaking transactional consistency when called multiple times in sequence.
findings.evidence: await db.commit() # Called inside _update_status() on lines 230, 237, 240
findings.consequence: Partial failures leave documents in inconsistent state; no rollback capability
findings.fix: Remove db.commit() from _update_status() and let _process_job() control transaction boundaries

findings.title: Missing retry_count validation
findings.description: retry_count from job payload is used directly without validation.
findings.evidence: retry_count = job.get("retry_count", 0) # No validation for negative or extremely large values
findings.consequence: Malicious jobs could cause denial of service via resource exhaustion
